candidate_result_rows.claim: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATION (o36): that holds for every VALUE a state file can hold, and a corrupt .failcount costs at most one extra link because finalize() overwrites it with a plain decimal on the next failure (harness X8: abc, then 2, then 4 and the breaker on link 2; X8b at the slow-failure floor trips on link 3; X9: the corrupt value persists only across scheduler-terminated links, with a WARNING each). It does NOT hold when the file cannot be WRITTEN: no write of .failcount or .chain_depth is checked, so a .failcount that is a directory, unreadable or read-only is read as 0 (no WARNING when cat fails) and never advances -- every link prints 'chain continues' and queues its successor, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN (X3, X4, X5); the same fail-open direction applies to the operator knobs, which are not read through read_counter: KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test false so the breaker never trips (X10b: 2, 4, 6 with a successor each link) and KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound (X10c); KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual). The loop's own CHANGE 10 writer carries the same trim / guard / width / 10# parse, so a seeded 08 self-heals to 9 on the next completed cycle instead of killing the loop after every cycle. No writer in codes/ can produce a padded value in the first place (no printf %0Nd, no seq -w; every write is an unpadded $(( )) result), so the exposure only ever needed a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Nothing here ran on a GPU or under a real scheduler.

metric_breakdown._definition: distinct failure / termination paths shown offline to end the link the way the claim says, 22 = 11 + 4 + 4 + 3
wrapper_classes_unchanged_from_the_admit: deliberate storage stop (loop exit 3 with STOP): successor cancelled, no attempt spent
scheduler termination seen as SIGTERM to this wrapper: successor kept, count untouched
scheduler termination seen as loop status 143 past KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS: successor kept
pre-flight failure: counted with the fast-failure penalty, successor cancelled
loop failure: counted, successor cancelled only when the breaker trips
loop exit 3 with no STOP: counted as an ordinary failure
exit 0 before the loop started (STOP at entry): count left
breaker trip: .breaker_tripped written and the queued successor scancelled
post-trip guard: a link that starts with the breaker tripped exits without running the loop
SIGKILL: no handler, nothing written, successor kept -- shown, not claimed as handled (scenario M)
wrapper_classes_added_by_the_third_repai: SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight: the loop is not launched, the link exits 143 as a scheduler termination
loop failure recorded before a later SIGTERM: counted as the failure, not waved through as the signal
scheduler termination on a link that completed cycles: the failure run is cleared
failure on a link that completed cycles: the failure run restarts before the new failure is counted
loop_script_staging_paths_added_by_the_t: failing cp in the staging section with KTG_STAGE_ONLY=1: exit 1, nothing staged (was exit 0 with a broken archive)
failing cp in the staging section with no KTG_STAGE_ONLY: exit 1 before cycle 1 (was cycle 1 out of the broken archive)
unreadable but present config: exit 1 at the cp (was a staged archive with no selfplay.cfg)
missing config: exit 2 from the explicit check, unchanged, proving the explicit guards were not disturbed
state_file_paths_added_by_this_repair (3: corrupt or leading-zero .cycles_completed at entry or in finalize: the count is written, .breaker_tripped is written and the queued successor is cancelled for every seed (was: finalize abandoned at :233 on 08/09, count left, successor kept -- the o26 class)

corrupt .failcount: read as its base-10 value or as 0 with a WARNING line, finalize still classifies and still writes (was: abc aborted finalize with "unbound variable" and left the successor queued; 0x10 was read as 16 and 99999999999999999999 wrapped to 7766279631452241921, both tripping the breaker on a wrong number)

corrupt .chain_depth: read as its base-10 value or as 0 with a WARNING line, the link continues and the successor is queued (was: 08 killed the wrapper at :141 with "value too great for base" then ":142 chaindepth: unbound variable" BEFORE the resubmit, so the chain ended silently with no successor at all -- a path o35's statement did not record)
